pl-l3d19c2-d1e114.summary: Explains that he became mortal man to conquer the devil by dying. If a man did not conquer him, man would seem taken from him unjustly by violence, having freely submitted to him; if a man conquered him, he lost man by clear right. For a man to conquer, God had to be in him to make him immune from sin; a man by himself, or an angel in a man, would easily sin, since both natures are known to have fallen. So the Son of God took a passible man and tasted death in him, opening heaven and redeeming us from the devil's slavery, i.e., sin, and from penalty.
claims: A man had to conquer the devil for the victory to be just.
God had to be in that man to keep him sinless.

pl-l3d19c2.summary: Explains that God became mortal man in order to conquer the devil by dying: if a man did not conquer him, man would seem taken from him by violence rather than justice, since man had freely submitted; if a man conquered him, he lost man by clear right. For a man to conquer, God had to be in him to keep him free of sin, since a mere man or an angel in a man would easily sin, both natures having fallen. So the Son took a passible man, tasted death, opened heaven, and redeemed us from the devil's slavery, which is sin, and from penalty.
claims: A man had to conquer the devil for the victory to be just.
God had to be in that man to keep him free from sin.
A mere man or an angel would easily sin.
